units.title: The empirical second moment is an average of rank-one operators
units.statement: For a finite sample x_i in a real inner-product space, the empirical second-moment operator is the inverse sample size times the sum of y ↦ ⟪x_i,y⟫x_i. The empty-sample convention is zero; concentration consumers use a nonempty index type.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space and I is a finite type.
The sample is an arbitrary function I→E.
No probability law, independence, centering, or boundedness is assumed by the definition.

steps.title: Turn each vector into a rank-one operator
steps.text: The Mathlib rank-one operator sends y to the inner product with x_i multiplied by x_i.

steps.title: Average the finite family
steps.text: Sum the continuous linear maps and scale by the inverse real cardinality.
steps.lean: Continuous linear maps carry finite sums and real scalar multiplication.

units.lean_statement: Lean keeps the real inner-product space, finite sample index, and empty-sample inverse-cardinality convention explicit.
units.lean_proof: This is a transparent definition; no theorem or probabilistic premise is hidden in it.
units.boundary: This definition is an empirical second moment. Calling it a covariance requires an appropriate centering convention, supplied separately by the consumer.

units.title: A self outer product has operator norm equal to the squared vector norm
units.statement: For every vector x in a real inner-product space, the continuous rank-one operator y ↦ ⟪x,y⟫x has operator norm exactly ‖x‖².
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.
x is arbitrary; finite dimensionality and completeness are not assumed.

steps.title: Use the rank-one norm identity
steps.text: Mathlib computes the norm of u⊗v as ‖u‖‖v‖.
steps.lean: Simplify InnerProductSpace.rankOne with its norm theorem.

steps.title: Rewrite the product as a square
steps.text: The identical norm factors are exactly ‖x‖².

units.lean_statement: The equality is stated directly for Mathlib's continuous rank-one operator.
units.lean_proof: The proof uses the library norm formula and the definition of a square.
units.boundary: This is deterministic Hilbert-space operator algebra; it contains no concentration claim.

units.title: Empirical covariance is reduced to bounded symmetric centered summands
units.statement: For a nonempty finite sample with ‖x_i‖≤B, a symmetric population operator Σ with ‖Σ‖≤B², and B≥0, the empirical error is the average of x_i⊗x_i−Σ; every summand is symmetric and has operator norm at most 2B².
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space and I is a nonempty finite type.
B is nonnegative and every sample vector has norm at most B.
The supplied population continuous linear operator is symmetric and has norm at most B².
No independence, expectation, variance proxy, tail theorem, or dimension bound is assumed.

steps.title: Expand the centered finite sum
steps.text: Distribute the finite sum over subtraction. Nonemptiness makes the sample cardinality nonzero, so inverse scaling cancels the repeated population term.

steps.title: Preserve symmetry under centering
steps.text: Each x_i⊗x_i is symmetric, and the difference of symmetric operators is symmetric.

steps.title: Bound each centered summand
steps.text: The triangle inequality, the exact rank-one norm, ‖x_i‖≤B, and ‖Σ‖≤B² yield the standard 2B² bound.
steps.lean: Use norm_sub_le, norm_rankOne_self_eq_sq, monotonicity of squaring on nonnegative reals, and ring normalization.

units.lean_statement: All boundedness, symmetry, nonemptiness, and normalization assumptions are explicit, and the conclusion is a three-part conjunction.
units.lean_proof: The proof performs the exact finite-sum cancellation, transports symmetry through subtraction, and combines the triangle inequality with the exact rank-one norm.
units.boundary: This theorem prepares a matrix-concentration input. It does not prove matrix Bernstein, choose a variance proxy, establish independence, or derive a probability tail or sample complexity.

units.title: A unit-vector covariance has an exact centered operator second moment
units.statement: Let X be a unit-vector-valued map such that X⊗X is Bochner integrable, and let C be the Bochner expectation of X⊗X. Then C is self-adjoint, ‖C‖≤1, E[(X⊗X-C)²]=C-C², and ‖C-C²‖≤2‖C‖.
units.formula: C=\mathbb E[X\otimes X],\quad C^*=C,\quad \|C\|\le1,\quad \mathbb E[(X\otimes X-C)^2]=C-C^2,\quad \|C-C^2\|\le2\|C\|
assumptions: E is a complete real inner-product space and μ is a probability measure.
X has norm exactly one at every point; no almost-everywhere weakening is hidden.
The rank-one operator X⊗X is Bochner integrable and its integral is the supplied population operator C.
No independent sample family, dimension, matrix exponential, or concentration theorem is assumed.

steps.title: Integrate rank-one symmetry
steps.text: Every self outer product is symmetric. Evaluation and the real inner product commute with the Bochner integral, so the expectation C is self-adjoint.
steps.lean: Use isSymmetric_rankOne_self, ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply, integral_inner, and isSelfAdjoint_iff_isSymmetric.

steps.title: Bound the population operator
steps.text: The Bochner integral norm is at most the integral of the pointwise operator norm. Unit norm makes ‖X⊗X‖=1, and a probability measure gives total mass one.

steps.title: Expand the centered square
steps.text: A unit-vector outer product is an idempotent projection. Expanding the noncommutative square and commuting left and right multiplication with integration turns both cross terms into C².
steps.lean: Use isStarProjection_rankOne_self, noncomm_ring, integral_sub/add, and ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm.

steps.title: Control the variance operator
steps.text: Submultiplicativity gives ‖C²‖≤‖C‖². Since ‖C‖≤1, the triangle inequality yields ‖C-C²‖≤2‖C‖.
steps.lean: Use norm_sub_le, norm_pow_le', hNorm, and real arithmetic.

units.lean_statement: The conclusion is a four-part conjunction and all probability, integrability, unit-norm, and population-identification assumptions occur explicitly in the signature.
units.lean_proof: The proof integrates pointwise rank-one symmetry, applies the Bochner norm bound, expands the noncommutative centered square using rank-one idempotence, commutes multiplication through the integral, and finishes with the operator-norm triangle inequality.
units.boundary: This is the expectation-level moment calculation immediately before matrix Bernstein. It does not establish independence, an operator MGF bound, a trace inequality, a tail estimate, or sample complexity.
